data.gender_notes: Ashvathama is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ashvathama is a name derived from the Sanskrit words ‘ashva’ meaning horse and ‘tama’ meaning born. This name is given to a boy born on a horse or to a warrior who rides a horse into battle. In Hindu mythology, Ashvathama is the name of a great warrior who fought in the Mahabharata war. The name Ashvathama carries the meaning “Horse-born” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi, Marathi. Parents who choose Ashvathama usually hope their child will grow to embody horse-born and live with faith, good character and purpose.

The curse turns Ashvathama into an immortal being who can only be killed by a Kshatriya warrior who has performed the last rites for his father.
